what_it_does: This paper describes a high-speed driver circuit for optical fiber communication (specifically for pluggable optics modules used in data centers). The driver must send signals at 100 billion bits per second while maintaining large voltage swings for signal reliability, high amplification, and wide bandwidth—a hard trade-off in conventional designs. The innovation is to use transmission lines (patterns of wires on the chip) in a cross-folded arrangement that simultaneously amplify the signal and equalize it (correct distortion from the fiber) using five adjustable taps that reshape the signal automatically.
